title: The Lowdown on Anonymous
summary: Josh and Chuck explain Anonymous, the loosely organized hacktivist collective that grew out of the 4chan image boards. They cover its origins on 4chan and the random board (/b/), early trolling and the Hal Turner and Project Chanology operations against Scientology, Operation Payback (WikiLeaks-related DDoS attacks on Visa, MasterCard, PayPal), DDoS attacks and the Low Orbit Ion Cannon, government prosecution of hackers, Arab Spring involvement, Steubenville rape case exposure, the Ku Klux Klan data dump, HBGary/Aaron Barr, and how the group is structured and how people get involved. The episode closes with listener mail from a UK listener and a sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and overview of Anonymous
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about the office work party and their limited expertise. They introduce Anonymous as a hacker activist group, note its key characteristics (no self-disclosure, moral stances, physical presence, branding with Guy Fawkes masks), and mention the Tupac fake news hoax by the offshoot WollSec.

segments.title: Podcast ad for The Message
segments.summary: Sponsor read promoting the GE Podcast Theater and Panoply series The Message.

segments.title: Origins on 4chan and the Hal Turner operation
segments.summary: Anonymous grew out of 4chan, founded in 2003 by Christopher Poole, and its random board. Members who liked trolling later split between pranks and moral causes. Their campaign against racist radio host Hal Turner, after he published prank caller information, led to his going off air.

segments.title: Project Chanology against Scientology
segments.summary: In 2008 Anonymous targeted Scientology after it tried to remove the Tom Cruise video from the Internet. Tactics included a Google bomb, prank pizza orders, black faxes, and calls for physical protests at churches. Hosts note the operations were framed as responses to Internet censorship and rule breaking.

segments.title: Operation Payback, DDoS attacks, and government hypocrisy
segments.summary: Operation Payback in 2010 attacked Visa, MasterCard, and PayPal after they stopped WikiLeaks donations. The hosts explain DDoS attacks and the Low Orbit Ion Cannon, and note that prosecutors punished individuals for DDoS while the US government used the same tactics. A Scientology-related arrest is described along with lawyer Tor Ekeland's criticism of harsh hacker sentencing.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Short break between segments with a brief transition.

segments.title: Other operations: Westboro, Arab Spring, Steubenville, LulzSec
segments.summary: The hosts cover Anonymous actions against Westboro Baptist Church, its role in the Arab Spring including Egypt's internet shutdown, the Steubenville rape case exposure, and the LulzSec fifty days of mayhem, including the Magnets.com episode.

segments.title: Membership, structure, leadership, and notable cases
segments.summary: Anonymous has no formal membership, and joining through forums can be dangerous. Members are often arrested, as with Jeremy Hammond and Barrett Brown. Only about a fifth are hackers, per Gabriella Coleman. The group has no hierarchy though informal leaders emerge. Also covered: the Ku Klux Klan data dump, the HBGary and Aaron Barr episode, and the 4chan origin of the name.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: Listener mail from a UK listener celebrating their podcast milestone, followed by discussion of the hosts' chemistry and the sign-off.
